Yet streaming understanding must also be closed-loop: task-relevant evidence may require both recalling past observations and actively acquiring new views. Existing streaming approaches largely emphasize processing incoming observations, leaving task-driven active exploration underexplored. We introduce MemAct, a framework for streaming spatial understanding with memory and action. A shared vision--language model incrementally writes structured historical memory, retrieves records and past frames on demand, and acquires additional evidence through movement and turning. Retrieved evidence and action observations inform subsequent decisions, enabling the agent to continue exploring or answer within a unified reasoning loop. We develop the MemAct suite, a data generation pipeline and collection across real and simulated environments, with approximately 1M training examples for spatial reasoning, memory writing, retrieval, and exploration. Its MemAct-bench comprises 20,000 main QA pairs evaluating current-observation understanding, historical evidence use, and active exploration, plus 2,000 separate Timing questions. MemAct combines supervised fine-tuning for memory and interaction with counterfactual action optimization using cumulative evidence gains, action costs, and terminal answer quality to improve exploration and stopping decisions. Experiments show that MemAct outperforms existing spatial understanding and streaming baselines and approaches frontier multimodal models on MemAct-bench while retaining streaming inference efficiency.
tldr: MemAct is a framework for streaming spatial understanding in embodied agents, combining memory writing/retrieval, active exploration, and counterfactual action optimization in a unified VLM reasoning loop, outperforming baselines on its MemAct-bench.
tldr_zh: MemAct是一种用于具身代理流式空间理解的框架，结合记忆写入/检索、主动探索和反事实动作优化于统一的VLM推理循环中，在MemAct-bench上优于基线。
summary_zh: 空间理解对于具身智能体在物理世界中的导航与交互至关重要。由于观测数据是逐步到达的，智能体必须以流式方式推理。然而，流式理解也必须是闭环的：与任务相关的证据既可能需要回顾过去的观测，也需要主动获取新的视角。现有的流式方法主要侧重于处理传入的观测，而任务驱动的主动探索尚未得到充分研究。我们提出了MemAct，一个结合记忆与动作的流式空间理解框架。一个共享的视觉-语言模型增量式地写入结构化历史记忆，按需检索记录和过去的帧，并通过移动和转向获取额外证据。检索到的证据和动作观测为后续决策提供信息，使智能体能够在统一的推理循环中继续探索或回答问题。我们开发了MemAct套件，包括一个数据生成流水线和跨真实及模拟环境的数据集，包含约100万个训练样本，涵盖空间推理、记忆写入、检索和探索。其MemAct基准测试包含20，000个主要问答对，评估当前观测理解、历史证据使用和主动探索，以及2，000个独立的时间问题。MemAct将监督微调用于记忆和交互，并结合基于累积证据增益、动作成本和最终答案质量的反事实动作优化，以改进探索和停止决策。实验表明，MemAct在MemAct基准上优于现有的空间理解和流式基线方法，并接近前沿多模态模型的性能，同时保持了流式推理的效率。

title: Collaborative Planning for UAV-UGV Teams under Operational Constraints via Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion
summary: Collaborative planning under operational constraints is essential for heterogeneous robot teams in large-scale missions. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) provide rapid area coverage but are limited by onboard energy, while Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) can serve as mobile recharging stations yet are constrained by road-network traversability. Effective collaboration must enforce operational constraints during execution while enabling parallel, coordinated actions. Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) have shown promise through token unmasking but have two key limitations: entropy-guided scheduling assumes distributional alignment and reliance on differentiable constraints for diffusion-time optimization. We propose Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion (MEND), which formulates collaborative planning as a conditional masked generative process to generate context-aware action sequences for UAV-UGV teams. MEND introduces a neuro-symbolic diffusion paradigm that constrains conditional masked diffusion policies at execution by reweighting the learned action distribution with a logic-induced admissibility indicator, thereby enforcing compliance with operational constraints. MEND introduces an error-bounded inference scheduling at execution that constructs the unmasking schedule by selecting positions with minimal predictive entropy over the constraint-aware action distribution, enhancing collaborative planning optimality under operational constraints. Extensive experimental results in simulation, on real-world maps, and with physical robot teams demonstrate that MEND advances UAV-UGV collaborative planning under operational constraints.
tldr: MEND formulates collaborative UAV-UGV planning as a conditional masked generative process with neuro-symbolic constraints and error-bounded inference scheduling, improving compliance and optimality under operational constraints in simulation and physical tests.
tldr_zh: MEND 将无人机-无人车协同规划建模为条件掩码生成过程，并通过神经符号约束和误差有界推理调度，在仿真和实物测试中提升操作约束下的合规性与最优性。
summary_zh: 在操作约束下的协同规划对于大规模任务中的异构机器人团队至关重要。无人机（UAV）能够提供快速的区域覆盖，但受到机载能量的限制，而无人地面车辆（UGV）可作为移动充电站，却受限于道路网络的可通行性。有效的协同必须在执行过程中强制执行操作约束，同时支持并行、协调的行动。掩码扩散模型（MDMs）已通过令牌去掩码展现出潜力，但存在两个关键局限：基于熵的调度假设分布对齐，以及依赖可微约束进行扩散时优化。我们提出了掩码误差有界神经符号扩散（MEND），将协同规划建模为条件掩码生成过程，以生成无人机-无人地面车辆团队的情境感知行动序列。MEND引入了一种神经符号扩散范式，通过用逻辑诱导的可接受性指示器对学习到的动作分布进行重新加权，在执行阶段约束条件掩码扩散策略，从而确保符合操作约束。MEND在执行阶段引入了误差有界推理调度，通过在约束感知的动作分布上选择预测熵最小的位置来构建去掩码调度，从而在操作约束下提升协同规划的最优性。在仿真、真实地图以及物理机器人团队上的大量实验结果表明，MEND在操作约束下推动了无人机-无人地面车辆协同规划的进步。

title: Mobility-Budget-Constrained Submodular Maximization for Distributed Semantic Multi-Robot Exploration
summary: Multi-robot exploration under communication and mobility constraints requires balancing information gain with reachability. We present a distributed semantic exploration framework that combines Dirichlet mapping, budget-constrained trajectory selection, and Resource-Aware distributed Greedy (RAG) coordination. Each robot clusters frontiers, computes terrain- and heading-aware least-cost paths with a single budget-limited Dijkstra search, and selects feasible paths by marginal information gain, represented by the expected reduction in Dirichlet entropy. Each robot's per-round selection is exact, the team's joint per-round information gain is at least half the centralized optimum, and the bound degrades gracefully under limited communication. Ten-run gridworld ablations show improved coverage, semantic mIoU, and map certainty with lower entropy and traversal cost per unit distance than shortest-distance frontier selection. Budget-sensitivity experiments show that an intermediate budget best balances path reach and receding-horizon execution. In photorealistic full-system simulation against five coordination rules run in their native published forms, the proposed method attains the highest mean coverage and semantic accuracy while being the only one that respects the per-trajectory mobility budget.
tldr: This paper introduces a distributed semantic multi-robot exploration framework that uses Dirichlet mapping, budget-constrained trajectory selection, and a resource-aware greedy coordination algorithm to balance information gain with mobility constraints, achieving improved coverage and semantic accuracy in simulations.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种分布式语义多机器人探索框架，结合Dirichlet映射、预算受限轨迹选择和资源感知贪心协调算法，在移动性约束下平衡信息增益，并在仿真中提高了覆盖率和语义精度。
summary_zh: 在通信与移动性约束下的多机器人探索任务中，需在信息增益与可达性之间寻求平衡。我们提出了一种分布式语义探索框架，该框架融合了狄利克雷映射、预算受限的轨迹选择以及资源感知的分布式贪心（RAG）协调机制。每个机器人对前沿进行聚类，通过单次预算受限的Dijkstra搜索计算考虑地形与航向的最小代价路径，并依据边际信息增益（以狄利克雷熵的预期减少量表示）选择可行路径。每个机器人每轮的选择是精确的，团队每轮联合信息增益至少达到集中式最优值的一半，且在通信受限条件下该界会优雅退化。十次网格世界消融实验表明，相较于最短距离前沿选择方法，本方法在覆盖率、语义mIoU和地图确定性方面均有提升，同时降低了熵值和单位距离的遍历代价。预算敏感性实验显示，中等预算能够在路径可达性与滚动时域执行之间达到最佳平衡。在与五种以原始发表形式运行的协调规则进行的光照逼真全系统仿真对比中，所提方法在平均覆盖率和语义精度上均达到最高，并且是唯一满足每条轨迹移动性预算的方法。

title: Reference Wording Shapes Retrieval of Robot Task Instructions
summary: Identifying a robot task from a short instruction is sensitive to which descriptions are available for retrieval. We investigate this effect in the natural-language instructions included with the RLBench manipulation benchmark. We extract 296 fixed descriptions from 62 publicly available task files and compare five training-free lexical rankers over 80 random choices of one indexed description per task. Exact strings assigned to conflicting task labels are excluded from the primary score. Character n-gram TF-IDF achieves 61.3% mean top-1 accuracy on the resulting held-out instructions, compared with 55.6% for BM25 and 54.9% for word TF-IDF. Across gallery choices, character TF-IDF ranges from 55.2% to 66.8%; its 5th-95th percentile range is 56.9%-64.8%. Adding a second indexed description improves character TF-IDF by 7.0 percentage points on matched queries. These results quantify the influence of reference wording and representation choice on instruction-to-task retrieval under a consistent evaluation protocol.
tldr: This paper analyzes how the choice of reference wording affects retrieval of robot task instructions, comparing lexical rankers on RLBench and showing that character n-gram TF-IDF performs best.
tldr_zh: 本文分析了参考措辞的选择如何影响机器人任务指令的检索，在RLBench上比较了词法排序器，并显示字符n-gram TF-IDF表现最佳。
summary_zh: 从短指令中识别机器人任务，其效果高度依赖于可供检索的任务描述。本研究在RLBench操作基准所附的自然语言指令中考察了这一影响。我们从62个公开可用的任务文件中提取了296条固定描述，并在每个任务随机选择一条索引描述的条件下，对五种无需训练的词汇排序器进行了80次随机选择的比较。被指派给冲突任务标签的精确字符串被排除在主要评分之外。字符n-gram TF-IDF在留出指令上的平均Top-1准确率达到61.3%，而BM25为55.6%，词级TF-IDF为54.9%。在不同图库选择下，字符TF-IDF的准确率范围为55.2%至66.8%；其第5至第95百分位区间为56.9%至64.8%。增加第二条索引描述后，字符TF-IDF在匹配查询上的准确率提升了7.0个百分点。这些结果在一致的评估协议下，量化了参考措辞和表示选择对指令到任务检索的影响。

title: Sim4RAD: A MATLAB Toolkit for Design-Phase Sizing, Actuator Selection and URDF-Model Verification of Serial Robotic Arms
summary: Actuator sizing is an early and consequential decision: joint torque and velocity specifications fix the motors, gearboxes and brakes before any CAD model exists. Sim4RAD is a MATLAB toolkit for that phase and for the verification that follows it. It builds a rigid-body model from a handful of parameters, and four analyses supply the specification: a static analysis combining lever-arm sampling with a posture search, giving a rated torque at a chosen payload envelope and a reproducible peak torque; a dynamics pipeline that reshapes a trajectory under one of four constraints, including the actuator torque-speed envelope; a stochastic analysis over many random motions, so a specification rests on a class of motions, not one trajectory; and a workspace and dexterity analysis that separates where the arm can reach from how it can reach there. Replacing the synthesized model by a URDF file turns the same analyses to verification. A 7-DOF anthropomorphic arm is compared in three layouts differing in the shoulder axis order and in whether the last wrist joint is coaxial with the payload. The static demand at half arm length is nearly the same in all three, and it sizes the joints rather than the sampled motion; reordering the shoulder axes leaves the worst-case torque unchanged at 55 N m and the reachable volume within 8 percent. A last wrist joint coaxial with the payload removes its gravity torque, reduces the adjacent wrist joint by almost a third and cuts the last joint demand tenfold in a 5 m/s scan, at the price of dexterity (mean 0.570 to 0.348). The same arm needs 20 to 37 times more torque for a 5 m/s target than for a 2 s motion: the scenario, not the trajectory, must be fixed first. Verification should use the URDF model of the detailed design; the toolkit is available at https://github.com/LasterLi/Sim4RAD.
tldr: Sim4RAD is a MATLAB toolkit for early-stage sizing, actuator selection, and URDF-based verification of serial robotic arms, demonstrated on a 7-DOF arm across three shoulder/layout configurations.
tldr_zh: Sim4RAD 是一个 MATLAB 工具箱，用于串联机械臂设计阶段的尺寸确定、执行器选型和基于 URDF 的验证，并在三种肩部/布局配置的七自由度机械臂上进行了演示。
summary_zh: 执行器选型是一个早期且影响深远的决策：在CAD模型存在之前，关节扭矩和速度规格便已确定了电机、减速箱和制动器。Sim4RAD是一个MATLAB工具包，专为此阶段及其后的验证工作而设计。它通过少量参数构建刚体模型，并通过四种分析提供设计规格：一是静力学分析，结合力臂采样与姿态搜索，在选定负载包络下给出额定扭矩和可复现的峰值扭矩；二是动力学流程，通过四种约束之一（包括执行器扭矩-速度包络）对轨迹进行整形；三是随机分析，覆盖大量随机运动，使规格基于一类运动而非单条轨迹；四是工作空间与灵巧度分析，将机械臂可达区域与到达方式分开评估。将合成模型替换为URDF文件后，同一套分析便可用于验证。一个7自由度拟人臂在三种布局下进行比较，区别在于肩部轴顺序以及最后一个腕关节是否与负载同轴。在三种布局中，半臂长处的静态需求几乎相同，且该需求决定关节尺寸而非采样运动；调换肩部轴顺序后，最坏情况扭矩保持55 N·m不变，可达体积差异在8%以内。使最后一个腕关节与负载同轴可消除其重力扭矩，使相邻腕关节需求降低近三分之一，并在5 m/s扫描运动中使末关节需求降为十分之一，但代价是灵巧度下降（均值从0.570降至0.348）。同一机械臂实现5 m/s目标所需的扭矩是完成2 s运动的20至37倍：必须先确定工况场景，而非具体轨迹。验证应使用详细设计的URDF模型；该工具包可在https://github.com/LasterLi/Sim4RAD获取。

title: Order-Consistent Latent Geometry for Reliable Short-Horizon Planning in World Models
summary: Latent planners often rank candidate action sequences by terminal Euclidean distance to a goal latent. Exact agreement with transition distance would make this score ideal, but is stronger than planning requires: along a transition-shortest rollout, the essential requirement is that latent distance does not reverse true transition progress. We show that this pathwise no-reversal requirement is precisely the classical self-approaching condition. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to identify self-approachingness as a planner-facing compatibility condition for terminal Euclidean latent planning and to connect its violation to an exact finite-horizon candidate-order reversal. Because visual world models predict discrete latent sequences, we analyze their polygonal interpolation. We prove that an acute bend creates a nonempty region in which terminal Euclidean distance ranks a transition-worse candidate ahead of one that makes genuine progress, even under exact rollouts. We further interpret latent dimension as angular capacity through a classical spherical-code bound. A controlled six-branch experiment, including a zero-padded three-dimensional baseline, validates the predicted ordering failure and separates angular arrangement from ambient dimensionality.
tldr: This paper identifies a pathwise no-reversal condition (self-approachingness) for terminal Euclidean latent planning in world models, proving that acute bends in discrete latent sequences cause candidate-order reversals and validating this with a controlled experiment.
tldr_zh: 本文为世界模型中的终端欧氏潜在规划提出路径无反转（自逼近）条件，证明离散潜在序列中的锐角弯曲导致候选排序反转，并通过受控实验验证。
summary_zh: 潜在规划器通常通过候选动作序列到目标潜在表征的终点欧氏距离来对其进行排序。若该距离与转移距离完全一致，则此评分标准是理想的，但这超出了规划所需的强度：沿转移最短轨迹，基本要求是潜在距离不得逆转真实的转移进度。我们证明，这一路径上的无逆转要求恰恰是经典的自接近条件。据我们所知，我们是首个将自接近性视为面向规划器的终端欧氏潜在规划兼容条件，并将其违反与精确的有限视界候选顺序反转联系起来的研究。由于视觉世界模型预测离散潜在序列，我们分析了它们的多边形插值。我们证明，即使在前向精确展开的情况下，一个锐角弯曲也会产生一个非空区域，在该区域内，终端欧氏距离会将转移更差的候选排在真正取得进展的候选之前。我们进一步通过经典的球面码界将潜在维度解释为角度容量。一项受控的六分支实验（包括一个零填充的三维基线）验证了预测的排序失效，并将角度排列与环境维度分离开来。

title: AffectWorld: Benchmarking Emotion-Driven Future World Prediction
summary: The world encompasses both physical environments and human actors. Predicting its evolution requires understanding both physical laws and how emotions shape human actions. However, existing world model benchmarks primarily assess physical plausibility and perceptual quality, leaving emotion-driven world evolution largely untested.We introduce AffectWorld, a benchmark that evaluates the chain Emotion-Action-World State through three tasks: World-State Consistency, Emotion-Action Consistency, and Causal Consistency. It comprises 1,498 everyday video samples annotated with plausible emotions, action tendencies, and atomic world-state constraints. A counterfactual subset of 233 samples tests whether changing an agent's emotion under fixed scene and event conditions yields corresponding changes in actions and consequences. We define eight metrics across the three tasks and an additional counterfactual metric, combining automatic visual assessment with human-calibrated VLM/LLM judgments. Evaluations of five SoTA world models (e.g., Cosmos3) required world-state change scores of 0.100-0.280 and counterfactual emotion sensitivity scores of 0.027-0.070 on a [0, 1] scale. These results reveal substantial gaps in generating the consequences of emotion-driven actions and adapting future predictions to emotional interventions. AffectWorld provides a testbed for advancing world models that capture how emotions shape future physical and social states.
tldr: AffectWorld is a new benchmark for evaluating emotion-driven future world prediction in world models, introducing tasks and metrics to test emotion-action-world state consistency and counterfactual reasoning.
tldr_zh: AffectWorld 是一个用于评估世界模型中情绪驱动的未来世界预测的新基准，通过任务和指标测试情绪-行动-世界状态一致性及反事实推理。
summary_zh: 世界既包含物理环境，也包含人类行为主体。预测其演变既需要理解物理规律，也需要理解情感如何塑造人类行为。然而，现有的世界模型基准主要评估物理合理性和感知质量，情感驱动的世界演变在很大程度上尚未得到检验。我们引入了 AffectWorld，一个通过三项任务评估“情感—行为—世界状态”链条的基准：世界状态一致性、情感—行为一致性和因果一致性。该基准包含 1，498 个日常视频样本，并标注了合理的情感、行为倾向和原子世界状态约束。其中包含 233 个反事实样本子集，用于测试在场景和事件条件固定的情况下，改变主体的情感是否会产生相应的行为及后果变化。我们在这三项任务上定义了八项指标，外加一项反事实指标，将自动视觉评估与经人工校准的 VLM/LLM 判断相结合。对五种最先进世界模型（如 Cosmos3）的评估结果显示，在 [0， 1] 尺度上，世界状态变化得分为 0.100—0.280，反事实情感敏感性得分为 0.027—0.070。这些结果揭示了当前模型在生成情感驱动行为后果以及使未来预测适应情感干预方面存在显著不足。AffectWorld 为推进能够捕捉情感如何塑造未来物理和社会状态的世界模型提供了一个测试平台。

title: RTISSLAM: In-air Imaging Sonar SLAM using a Robust Pose Graph and Occupancy Grid Mapping
summary: Sonar was one of the first sensors with which mobile robots built maps, and in-air sonar keeps working where cameras and lidar fail, in darkness, smoke, dust and next to glass. Classical sonar SLAM, however, relied on geometric features or occupancy grids built from sparse range readings, and both struggle with the specular reflections that dominate indoor sonar. In this letter, we introduce RTISSLAM, a novel sonar-only SLAM system for an embedded 3D imaging sonar, which combines the robust pose graph of BatSLAM 2.0 as back-end with an occupancy grid as map. Energyscapes from delay-multiply-and-sum beamforming with a range-wise CFAR serve as place descriptors for sequence-verified loop closures, acoustic odometry calibrates the wheel odometry online, recognized revisits are registered metrically, and the grid is stored per keyframe and anchored to the pose-graph nodes, so that it follows every loop closure. In simulated worlds with specular walls, RTISSLAM reduces the trajectory error of the wheel odometry from \SI{8.2}{\meter} to \SI{0.31}{\meter} in an office, while lidar-style grid SLAM on the same sonar data fails.
tldr: RTISSLAM is a sonar-only SLAM system for embedded 3D imaging sonar, combining a robust pose graph back-end with occupancy grid mapping. It uses energy-based place descriptors for loop closures and online acoustic odometry calibration, significantly reducing trajectory error in specular indoor environments where lidar-style grid SLAM fails.
tldr_zh: RTISSLAM 是一种仅使用声纳的 SLAM 系统，用于嵌入式 3D 成像声纳，结合了稳健的位姿图后端与占据栅格地图。它利用基于能量的位置描述符进行闭环检测和在线声学里程计校准，在镜面反射室内环境中显著降低轨迹误差，而激光雷达式栅格 SLAM 在此类数据上会失败。

title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms
summary: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) inspection is dominated by aerial surveys, which are effective for identifying module-level hot cells but provide limited visibility of critical components located under the array, including connectors, cabling, fasteners and structural elements. These assets are difficult to inspect consistently at scale, and their defects are often spatially small, partially occluded and difficult to localise from isolated images. We present an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system (Tricorder) for under-panel PV asset inspection. The approach combines LiDAR-inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) with geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal imagery and machine-learning-based object detection and segmentation. Detected assets are associated with the reconstructed 3D environment, allowing visual and thermal observations from multiple viewpoints to be spatially fused and localised. We demonstrate the approach on utility-scale PV data for MC4 connector detection and connection-state recognition, thermal anomaly identification, and detection of structural components including bolts, nuts and torque tubes. The results demonstrate a pathway from image-based inspection toward spatially grounded autonomous inspection, where defects are detected and linked to specific assets and their 3D locations within the solar farm.
tldr: This paper presents Tricorder, an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system for utility-scale solar farms, combining LiDAR-inertial SLAM, RGB and thermal imaging, and ML-based object detection to localize and fuse asset observations in 3D space.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了Tricorder，一个用于大型光伏电站的自动三维视觉-热成像检测系统，结合LiDAR惯性SLAM、RGB和热成像以及基于机器学习的物体检测，在三维空间中定位和融合资产观测。

title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
summary: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) processes the sequence in one forward pass. Causal attention, however, lets the hidden states of a part observe only the parts that precede it. LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation. One architecture thus handles semantic and geometric assembly and predicts all poses in a single non-autoregressive pass. LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate. Its advantage grows with the number of parts: at 100 parts it exceeds GARF by 33.5 points in part accuracy on Breaking Bad and Assembler by 29.1 points on PartNet, and it transfers zero-shot to unseen categories with more than 16 points higher part accuracy than the strongest of three baselines.
tldr: LLM2R casts 3D part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only LLM, using summary tokens and a part-aware pose head to predict all part poses in one pass, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and scaling to many parts.
tldr_zh: LLM2R 将三维零件装配视为序列建模，使用预训练的解码器 LLM，通过摘要令牌和零件感知姿态头一次性预测所有零件姿态，在准确性和多零件扩展性上达到最新水平。

title: APTree: Extended Behavior Trees for Adaptive and Scalable Automated Robotic Task Planning in Construction
summary: Task planning for robots in off-site construction prefabrication is primarily manual, leading to planning inefficiencies and reluctance to adopt robotic solutions. Existing approaches provide limited support for scalable, modular automated task planning and localized runtime replanning. This paper proposes APTree, a model-driven framework that integrates automated task planning with modular task execution using behavior trees as the execution model. APTree repeatedly applies and coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners to automatically generate and compose modular task plans at runtime. To support this approach, we develop a domain-specific language for the formal specification and validation of task plans, together with a compatible execution engine. We evaluate APTree on the real-world livMatS Biomimetic Shell pavilion, where it models the construction robotic fabrication domain, detects injected specification and planning errors at design time and runtime, and automatically generates large-scale task plans by coordinating three symbolic planners across numerous planning modules. A machine-checked formal analysis further shows that composed execution and local replanning are safe under explicitly stated assumptions, including planner soundness and non-interference of generated plans, providing practitioners with explicit conditions for dependable plan composition. APTree thus enables construction practitioners to leverage automated task planning without requiring detailed knowledge of symbolic planning techniques or APTree's internal implementation.
tldr: APTree is a model-driven framework using extended behavior trees and heterogeneous symbolic planners to automate task planning for construction robots, supporting modular execution and local replanning, evaluated on a real-world biomimetic shell pavilion.
tldr_zh: APTree是一个基于扩展行为树和异构符号规划器的模型驱动框架，用于实现建筑机器人的自动化任务规划，支持模块化执行和局部重规划，并在真实仿生外壳展馆上进行了评估。

title: Visual Sevoing from Lines
summary: In this work, we present a fundamentally new approach to visual servoing using lines. It is based on a theoretical and geometrical study of the main line representations which allowed us to define a new representation, the so-called binormalized Plucker coordinates. They are particularly well suited to visual servoing. Indeed, they allow the definition of a proper image line alignment concept. The control law which realizes such an alignment has moreover several properties: partial decoupling between rotation and translation, analytical inversion of the motion equations and global asymptotic stability conditions. This control law was validated both in simulation and experimentally in the specific case of an orthogonal trihedron.
tldr: The paper introduces a new line representation, binormalized Plücker coordinates, for visual servoing, enabling a control law with partial decoupling, analytical inversion, and global asymptotic stability, validated in simulation and on an orthogonal trihedron.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种新的直线表示（双归一化Plücker坐标）用于视觉伺服，实现了具有部分解耦、解析求逆和全局渐近稳定性的控制律，并在模拟和正交三面体上进行了验证。

title: Contractor Filters
summary: We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry. We derive an exact nominal recursion and a guaranteed robust enclosure, with validated flow inclusions preserving soundness. Optional sub-paving compression then provides finite outer representations. CFs are evaluated against a robust particle filter on range-only and terrain-based localization under outliers, probabilistic model mismatch, association ambiguity, and multimodality. CFs retain the simulated truth in all tested configurations, while particle-filter reliability degrades under persistent bias and spatial aliasing. Contractor strength and compression budget control the trade-off between paving tightness and computational cost, while preserving the enclosure guarantee.
tldr: This paper proposes Contractor Filters, a set-membership filtering architecture for nonlinear state estimation under bounded uncertainties and outliers, representing feasible states symbolically via contractors and validated against particle filters on localization tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出承包商滤波器，一种用于有界不确定性和离群值下非线性状态估计的集合成员滤波架构，通过承包商符号化表示可行状态，并在定位任务上优于粒子滤波器。

title: Information-based Unified Design Framework for NMR Magnetic Tracking System
summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) magnetic tracking offers a promising alternative to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based localization for medical robotic guidance. However, scalar field measurements and field-aligned marker moments constrain position and orientation tracking, requiring careful configuration design. We present a unified information-based framework that uses local covariance analysis to evaluate receiver geometry, marker separation, and external source configuration in on/off-board NMR tracking. Numerical evaluation shows that planar-array precision depends jointly on receiver count and geometry, with triangular lattice arrays achieving the lowest best-case position uncertainty among the evaluated layouts for 9--20 receivers. Two spatially separated, field-aligned markers enable device-axis tracking, with predicted angular uncertainty below $2^\circ$ at the evaluated workspace center for suitable marker separations. We further establish point-dipole source--receiver duality, unifying the analysis of on/off-board NMR tracking. These
tldr: This paper presents an information-based framework for designing NMR magnetic tracking systems for medical robotic guidance, using local covariance analysis to optimize receiver geometry, marker separation, and source configurations.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于信息论的 NMR 磁跟踪系统设计框架，通过局部协方差分析优化接收器几何、标记物间距及源配置，用于医疗机器人引导。

title: A Minimum Exact Disjunctive Basis for Two-Robot Solvability Profiles
summary:
We completely characterize the solvability profiles of tasks for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under variable disorientation, chirality, and rigid movements. The four standard capability models and the schedulers considered here have a known quotient order Q of thirteen computational classes. A task's solvability profile is the set of classes in which it is solvable, and is necessarily an upset of Q. We prove that every upset is realizable and construct a minimum exact disjunctive basis of thirteen concrete tasks.
  The basis contains one task for each principal upset. For every antichain of Q, the disjunction of the corresponding tasks has profile exactly equal to the union of their profiles. This exactness is not implied by the individual profiles: an algorithm may satisfy different disjuncts in different executions. We establish it by constructing, for every algorithm in each maximal class outside the target union, a single admissible fair execution violating all selected predicates simultaneously. Consequently, the realizable profiles form the entire finite distributive lattice Up(Q): there are exactly 54 profiles, counted by the antichain polynomial 1 + 13z + 24z^2 + 16z^3, and each has a canonical disjunctive representation using at most three principal tasks.
  We also identify six tasks whose solvability signatures recover every inclusion and incomparability in Q, and prove that six is minimum even among arbitrary separating tasks. Their profiles are precisely the principal upsets generated by the join-irreducible elements of Q. In contrast, any task family generating every profile by exact disjunctions must contain all thirteen principal profiles. Thus our exact disjunctive basis has minimum size and is unique at the profile level.
tldr: This paper provides a complete characterization of solvability profiles for two autonomous mobile robots under various capability models, showing that all upsets are realizable and constructing a minimum exact disjunctive basis of thirteen tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文完整刻画了两个自主移动机器人在不同能力模型下的可解性轮廓，证明所有上集均可实现，并构造了包含十三个任务的最小精确析取基。

title: An Optimal Algorithm for Changing from Longitudinal to Latitudinal Formation of Autonomous Aircraft Squadrons
summary: This work presents an algorithm for changing from longitudinal to latitudinal formation of autonomous aircraft squadrons. The maneuvers are defined dynamically by using a predefined set of 3D basic maneuvers. This formation change is necessary when the squadron has to perform tasks demanding both formations, such as landing, lift-off, obstacle avoidance and georeferencing. The time complexity analysis of the transformation algorithm reveals that its efficiency is optimal. Simulations show that the formation change is done without collision, and the proof of correctness ensures its latitudinal formation features.
tldr: This paper presents an optimal algorithm for transforming autonomous aircraft squadrons from longitudinal to latitudinal formation using predefined 3D maneuvers, with collision-free simulation and correctness proof.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种最优算法，利用预定义三维基本机动，实现自主飞机中队从纵向编队到横向编队的无碰撞变换，并给出正确性证明。

title: Filtering for Liveness: Recurrence via Backup Reachability Control Barrier Functions
summary: Liveness requires a dynamical system to repeatedly accomplish a desired objective over time. In this work, we consider a particular form of liveness known as recurrence, which requires the closed-loop trajectory to regularly revisit a prescribed set, with no more than a specified amount of time between visits. Inspired by the control barrier function (CBF) safety-filter paradigm, we develop a controller-filtering framework that makes adjustments to a nominal controller only when necessary to guarantee recurrence. Unlike conventional CBF methods, which enforce set forward invariance, our framework allows the trajectory to leave the set while guaranteeing its timely return. To achieve this, our framework combines two components: a backup reachability CBF that preserves the ability to return to the prescribed set within the allowable time, and a timing-based mechanism that invokes a reaching controller only when the nominal behavior would otherwise fail to meet the return-time requirement. The resulting framework guarantees recurrence while preserving the nominal behavior when possible, enabling control objectives that require temporary excursions from the set, such as traversal between disjoint regions. Our method is successfully utilized in a drone racing example with a recurrence constraint on beacon visibility.
tldr: This paper introduces a control-barrier-function-based filtering framework that guarantees recurrence (timely revisiting of a set) by combining a backup reachability CBF and a timing-based switching mechanism, demonstrated on a drone racing beacon-visibility task.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于控制障碍函数的滤波框架，通过结合备份可达性CBF和基于时机的切换机制来保证回归性（及时重访集合），并在无人机竞速的灯塔可见性任务中得到验证。

title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
summary: This work studies certified reach-avoid control of stochastic hybrid systems in which a stochastic differential equation governs continuous flow and a controlled stochastic kernel governs guard-triggered resets. The input appears only in the reset kernel, where it determines the post-jump distribution. Certificates for such systems have so far assumed spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times, a finite horizon, or discrete-time dynamics; we certify, over the infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with at least a prescribed probability. First, we introduce reach-avoid contact certificates, whose flow and jump conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, and prove that any such certificate with a compatible reset policy meets the specification; a pointwise safety filter extends this guarantee from verification to control by constraining arbitrary nominal controllers. Next, we prove that executions are non-Zeno and bound the expected settling time and reset count. We frame certificate search as a linear program over any twice-differentiable dictionary followed by independent verification. We illustrate our approach via comparisons where the certified region is a subset covering 93.6\% of the ground truth and where our certificate-based safety filter reaches the goal while reducing collisions from 68 to zero across 200 episodes of a dribbling ball problem.
tldr: This paper introduces reach-avoid contact certificates for stochastic hybrid systems with control-dependent reset kernels, enabling infinite-horizon safety guarantees and a safety filter that reduces collisions in a dribbling ball problem.
tldr_zh: 本文针对控制相关重置核的随机混合系统，提出了可达-避免接触证书，实现了无限时域安全性保证，并通过安全过滤器在运球问题中将碰撞从68次降至0次。

title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
summary: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while keeping the encoder fixed. We evaluate RAN-JEPA using public operator performance data for pretraining and a real-equipment four-cell 5G testbed for domain adaptation, post-training, and control. Across four future 15-minute intervals, RAN-JEPA achieves lower action-conditioned prediction error than a GPT-2 world-model baseline and a mechanistic rule, while remaining close to a strong persistence reference. What-if evaluation further shows that the model produces distinct and coherent future trajectories under matched SLEEP and KEEP plans. In closed-loop control, RAN-JEPA consistently supports higher sleep ratios than the two baselines at comparable congestion cost. These results show that observation-first, action-conditioned learning can turn abundant passive telemetry and limited intervention data into a practical predictive model for energy-aware RAN control.
tldr: RAN-JEPA is an action-conditioned world model for energy-efficient mobile network control, which separates representation learning from intervention learning to leverage abundant passive telemetry and limited controlled data. It demonstrates improved prediction and control performance over baselines on a real 5G testbed.
tldr_zh: RAN-JEPA 是一种用于节能移动网络控制的动作条件世界模型，它将表示学习与干预学习分离，以利用丰富的被动遥测数据和有限的受控数据。在真实 5G 测试平台上，它展示了优于基线的预测和控制性能。

title: WorldRecon: Generative Multi-View Mesh Reconstruction for Large-Scale 3D World
summary: Reconstructing complete, high-quality meshes of large-scale scenes from unposed multi-view images requires faithful geometric grounding while plausibly completing surfaces that are unobserved or only sparsely captured. We present WorldRecon, a generative multi-view reconstruction framework for recovering complete, large-scale 3D scene meshes from unposed RGB images. WorldRecon uses a coarse, noisy global point cloud and camera poses estimated from the input images by a reconstruction model as a global scaffold for whole-scene generation and partitions it into overlapping spatial blocks. To robustly leverage these imperfect geometric priors, we equip the native 3D generative model TRELLIS.2 with a dedicated reconstruction-based conditioning architecture that generates each block from its local point-cloud crop and block-relevant image observations, producing sparse structure, detailed geometry, and PBR materials. To maintain scene-level coherence, we introduce neighbour-aware latent inpainting and a causal world-generation procedure that propagates structural, geometric, and material context across overlapping blocks. Together, these designs scale multi-view generative reconstruction to large-scale scenes, yielding coherent, unified meshes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WorldRecon achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance, reducing Chamfer distance by 14.9% and 43.1% while improving F-score by 17.3% and 12.0% over the strongest baselines on synthetic and real-world indoor scenes, respectively, thereby demonstrating faithful and complete generative reconstruction as well as strong sim-to-real generalization. Project page: https://kszpxxzmc.github.io/WorldRecon-website/.
tldr: WorldRecon is a generative multi-view mesh reconstruction framework that leverages noisy global point clouds and camera poses as a scaffold to generate coherent, large-scale 3D scene meshes with sparse structure, detailed geometry, and PBR materials, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction performance on synthetic and real-world indoor scenes.
tldr_zh: WorldRecon 是一个生成式多视图网格重建框架，利用有噪声的全局点云和相机位姿作为脚手架，生成具有稀疏结构、详细几何和 PBR 材质的大规模一致 3D 场景网格，在合成和真实室内场景上取得了最先进的性能。

title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Long-horizon agents often struggle to recover from failures whose causes lie several steps earlier, beyond what local reflection or backtracking can resolve. We introduce BELIEFWEAVER, a framework that combines persistent evidence across attempts with prospective reasoning over repair directions. It maintains a relational belief state over frontiers, attempts, observations, and checkpoints. Execution evidence updates related frontier priorities across attempts and rollback, while diagnostic evidence gates execution. An implicit world model (IWM) evaluates repair hypotheses, predicts progress, and identifies relations among frontiers to guide exploration. We further distill these recurring IWM reasoning components into a 9B student through supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation (OPD). Across three terminal-based benchmarks, BELIEFWEAVER improves aggregate final score by 5.1 percentage points over native Terminus-2 continuation, with positive trends in exploration efficiency. The distilled 9B student improves final score by 9.8 percentage points over the reported native baseline while reducing estimated teacher API cost by 54.8% relative to the matched teacher. These results show that persistent evidence and prospective reasoning can improve recovery in long-horizon agent tasks while substantially reducing reliance on teacher-model inference.
tldr: BELIEFWEAVER improves long-horizon agent failure recovery by maintaining a relational belief state over attempts and using an implicit world model to evaluate repair hypotheses, distilled into a 9B student that reduces teacher API cost while boosting performance on terminal-based benchmarks.
tldr_zh: BELIEFWEAVER 通过维护关系信念状态并使用隐式世界模型评估修复假设，改进了长期任务智能体的失败恢复，并将其蒸馏到 9B 学生模型，在降低教师 API 成本的同时提升了终端基准的性能。

title: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: In cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), agents must learn to coordinate their actions to achieve shared objectives. A key indicator of effective coordination is behavioral diversity, i.e., the agents' potential to enact distinct yet complementary control policies given the same set of observations. Although behavioral diversity can enable role specialization and richer joint behaviors, its appropriate level is highly context- and task-dependent and often costly to tune. We propose Adaptive Diversity Control (ADiCo), a two-timescale framework that adapts behavioral diversity online during training. On a fast timescale, Diversity Control (DiCo) regulates system diversity toward a target value. On a slower timescale, an Extremum Seeking Controller (ESC) adjusts this target using only mean episodic returns, without requiring an explicit model or analytical gradient of the diversity-performance landscape. We evaluate ADiCo on six configurations across two cooperative MARL tasks, where it maintains task-appropriate diversity levels: low diversity when homogeneous policies are beneficial and higher diversity when heterogeneous policies are required. Through this adaptation, ADiCo matches or exceeds the mean performance of DiCo (best grid-searched diversity target) and Unconstrained DiCo (diversity allowed to emerge without target regulation). These results demonstrate that incorporating classical feedback control into MARL training enables effective coordination by providing a systematic alternative to task-specific manual selection of the diversity target.
tldr: ADiCo introduces a two-timescale framework that adapts behavioral diversity in multi-agent RL via extremum-seeking control, matching or exceeding grid-searched baselines without manual tuning.
tldr_zh: ADiCo 提出一种双时间尺度框架，通过极值搜索控制在线调整多智能体强化学习中的行为多样性，无需手动调参即可达到或超越网格搜索基线。

title: Augmenting Real-time Visualization in Minimally Invasive Surgery with Particle Filtering and Depth-Aware Occlusion Handling
summary: We present a real-time, hybrid framework for occlusion handling and depth-aware tracking in minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). Occlusions caused by surgical instruments often obscure the region of interest (ROI), affecting surgical precision. To address this, our approach integrates enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) based detection, Particle Filtering (PF), and monocular depth estimation using Multiple Depth Estimation Accuracy with Single Network (MiDaS). Occlusion is detected using a distance-based threshold between instruments and ROI. Experimental results demonstrate robust instrument detection with a confidence score of 0.85, effective occlusion event handling, and accurate depth prediction with an MAE of 0.34 cm and RMSE of 0.53 cm. Independent phantom-based validation against stereo depth measurements yielded an MAE of 0.65 cm and RMSE of 0.66 cm. The framework further achieved an occlusion detection accuracy of 81.95\% while maintaining real-time performance at 38.7 FPS. Preliminary surgeon feedback indicates that the proposed visualization framework is clinically relevant and holds promise for future intraoperative image-guided navigation and decision support in MIS.
tldr: A real-time hybrid framework for occlusion handling and depth-aware tracking in minimally invasive surgery, integrating YOLO detection, particle filtering, and MiDaS depth estimation.
tldr_zh: 一种用于微创手术中实时遮挡处理和深度感知跟踪的混合框架，集成了YOLO检测、粒子滤波和MiDaS深度估计。

title: From Orbit Matching to Docking: A Hierarchical Reinforcement-Learning Approach to Multiphase Rendezvous Trajectory Design
summary: As the complexity of space missions increases, autonomous spacecraft guidance must accommodate transitions between mission phases with distinct dynamics, objectives, and constraints. Rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) are particularly challenging because they span multiple operating regimes, from orbital-scale matching and far-range approach to close-range maneuvering and terminal docking. Existing reinforcement-learning approaches generally address only a subset of this sequence or rely on manually defined switching conditions between controllers. This study presents a hierarchical reinforcement-learning framework for autonomous, three-degree-of-freedom RPO that spans the complete trajectory from orbit matching to docking. Five specialized policies are trained for orbit matching, far-range approach, mid-range approach, close-range approach, and docking. A learned high-level manager policy then selects among these phase-specific controllers based on the evolving spacecraft state. The hierarchical approach is evaluated over the full end-to-end rendezvous sequence and compared with a fixed sequential-invocation heuristic to assess trajectory performance and transition behavior. Training and inference metrics are also analyzed for the individual phase policies and the complete hierarchical system.
tldr: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement-learning framework for autonomous spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations, training five specialized phase policies and a learned manager to select among them for full end-to-end trajectory design from orbit matching to docking.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于自主航天器交会与接近操作的分层强化学习框架，训练了五个专门的分阶段策略和一个学习型管理器，以选择它们完成从轨道匹配到对接的全端到端轨迹设计。

title: A Sense of Proprioception in Language Models
summary: In humans, proprioception corresponds to the sense of self-movement or position, e.g. understanding the position of one's arm. This sense is often less well-understood and in popular understanding sometimes conflated with introspection. But, notably, proprioception is a separate sense, with dedicated receptors and verifiable outcomes. On the other hand though, language models cannot observe their own internal states during training (and for example answer the question which experts activated in a certain layer of an MoE) and so cannot accurately report on them. Yet, such information is, by virtue of being internal to the model, both accessible, and readily constructed into verifiable signals. We argue that this provides the basis for a digital analog of proprioception. As such, we train models through SFT and on-policy training to equip them with this ability. We show that modern models can be trained to understand a range of subtypes of proprioception, such as routing decision awareness, token entropy, decision depth or logit lens information, without affecting model capabilities. We then run these models through a broad evaluation of situational awareness, legibility, and epiphenomenality, to evaluate in what ways access to proprioception changes model behavior.
tldr: This paper introduces a digital analog of proprioception for language models, training them to report internal states like routing decisions and token entropy without harming capabilities, and evaluating the behavioral effects of this access.
tldr_zh: 本文为语言模型引入了本体感觉的数字模拟，通过训练使模型能够报告路由决策、token熵等内部状态，且不影响模型能力，并评估了这种访问对模型行为的影响。

title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design
summary: Recent advances in zero-shot voice cloning systems make it possible to reproduce a recognizable voice from a short recording and attach it to arbitrary virtual characters. Prior work suggests that familiar vocal identity can carry over associated personality impressions to new targets such as robots or virtual characters. However, these works have mainly examined familiarity and personalization effects rather than directly testing whether a cloned familiar voice systematically transfers personality impressions to an embodied virtual character. Such transference raises the concern that cloned voices could be used to manipulate people into engaging with virtual characters as capable social actors. Across two studies, we investigated whether personality impressions transfer when a virtual character speaks with the cloned voice of a familiar person. Study 1 examined this question in a real-world university setting using the cloned voice of a lecturer familiar to the participating students. Study 2 examined the same question online using voices of social media content creators and members of their communities. Drawing on the concepts of identity activation, trait transfer, and person reconstruction, we show that evidence of personality transfer was limited in both studies. Observed effects were selective and did not generalize across traits or study contexts. In the online study in particular, recognizable voice identity cues activated expectations about the speaker but did not reconstruct the broader person impression. Qualitative responses further indicated that judgments were frequently shaped by perceived artificiality and by whether voice and appearance fit together. Our findings moderate common concerns that cloned voices straightforwardly manipulate people into perceiving artificial characters as capable social actors.
tldr: This paper tests whether cloned voices of familiar people transfer personality impressions to virtual characters, finding limited and selective evidence of transfer, which moderates concerns about voice cloning as a manipulation tool.
tldr_zh: 本文测试了熟悉声音的克隆是否能将个性印象转移到虚拟角色上，发现证据有限且具有选择性，从而缓和了关于声音克隆作为操纵工具的担忧。

title: Behavioural self-monitoring for autonomous earth observation agents: The attribute reliability monitor (ARM)
summary: Language and vision language models can support autonomous systems, but changing operating conditions may compromise the reliability of their semantic outputs. This work introduces the Attribute Reliability Monitor (ARM), a framework that accumulates evidence of suspicion over time to assess individual semantic attributes. ARM accommodates different detectors and temporal monitoring methods, while leaving intervention policies to the consuming system. An initial implementation was evaluated using a specialized vision language model developed for satellite thermal infrared imagery. Monitoring followed a black box approach, using only observable responses without access to internal model states, confidence scores, or external reference answers. Under controlled input degradation, disagreement between responses provided evidence for selective suspension of attributes. The results illustrate how external behavioral monitoring can inform continued use of model outputs, while distinguishing operational suspicion from semantic correctness.
tldr: Introduces a framework for monitoring the reliability of semantic attributes from language/vision-language models in autonomous Earth observation, using only observable responses to detect degradation and selectively suspend unreliable outputs.
tldr_zh: 提出一种框架，用于自主地球观测中语言/视觉语言模型语义属性的可靠性监控，仅通过可观测响应检测退化并选择性暂停不可靠输出。

title: Two Routes to Interoceptive Prioritisation: Dissociating Likelihood Precision and Preference Reweighting in Active Inference
summary: An embodied agent must prioritise among competing bodily needs. In active inference, it can respond to an urgent need by increasing the precision of information about that need or by increasing its preference for outcomes that relieve it. We compare these two interventions, separately and together, in a foraging gridworld with three lethal needs, and ask how each changes survival, perception and the body model the agent learns. Precision sharpens interoceptive posteriors and improves survival. Preference reweighting keeps bodily states further from their lethal boundaries and changes the states from which the agent learns, so its learned model covers fewer need levels, with lower quality across all levels but slightly higher quality on the levels it visits. An experiment on 72 further layouts does not establish the predicted preference benefit on difficult layouts, but both interventions improve average survival there and their interaction is positive. Survival alone therefore gives an incomplete account of how a model prioritises needs and learns about its body.
tldr: This paper studies active inference in a foraging gridworld, comparing two mechanisms for prioritizing bodily needs: precision sharpening of interoceptive signals versus preference reweighting. It finds that precision improves survival, while preference reweighting alters the learned body model and keeps states away from lethal boundaries, showing that survival alone incompletely captures model learning.
tldr_zh: 本文在觅食网格世界中研究主动推理，比较了两种优先处理身体需求的机制：增加内感受信号精度与调整偏好权重。发现精度可提高生存率，而偏好重加权会改变学习到的身体模型并使状态远离致命边界，表明仅靠生存率无法完整反映模型学习。

title: $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP: Plug-and-Play Denoising for Scientific Imaging with Self-Supervised Score Priors
summary: Modern image restoration methods increasingly rely on large-scale supervised training, yet clean targets are often prohibitively difficult to obtain in scientific imaging modalities such as hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Plug-and-play ADMM (PnP-ADMM) with pretrained diffusion priors offers a promising alternative, but the learned prior distribution can mismatch both the target scientific image distribution and the distribution of ADMM denoiser inputs induced by dual feedback. To mitigate these mismatches, we propose $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP, a self-supervised plug-and-play restoration framework that learns a score prior directly from observation-derived ADMM intermediate states, without clean training targets or externally pretrained weights. Specifically, the learned score corrects the input to the analytical prior update, combining observation-driven corrections with analytical regularization. We further analyze the convergence and reconstruction error of the corrected ADMM algorithm assuming an ideal score and quadratic data fidelity. Experiments on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising demonstrate consistent improvements over competing methods.

title: 4LC: 4D Latent Cache for Efficient Conditioning in Dynamic World Modeling
summary: For video generation in dynamic world modeling, observed static and dynamic content should be efficiently reused to provide conditions for repeated generation at different times and viewpoints. We introduce 4LC, a 4D latent cache with composite visual representations and a flexible spatiotemporal access interface. As a latent cache, 4LC directly reuses visual representations of static and dynamic content to provide generation conditions, avoiding per-request RGB rendering and re-encoding. As a composite cache, 4LC binds visual representations from multiple visual encoders (e.g., VAE, DINO, V-JEPA, VGGT) to shared geometry and motion, allowing the composite representations to describe the dynamic world with rich information. Besides, we design a flexible spatiotemporal interface, which directly reads the cache at independently specified times and viewpoints and combines readouts across observations, providing a common conditioning format for diverse downstream tasks. Building on 4LC, we develop 4LC-Video to address multiple video generation tasks through different configurations of source observations, spatiotemporal requests, and historical reuse, including camera control, temporal control, novel-view synthesis, scene revisits, and long-term generation. Our experiments show more efficient condition acquisition, effective spatiotemporal controllability, and scene consistency across tasks using a single 4LC-Video model without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: A CaLLM Judge is a Better Judge: Mitigating Bias in LLM-as-a-judge
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges to predict which of two candidate answers a human evaluator would prefer, providing a scalable alternative when human evaluation is too costly. Unfortunately, LLM judgments can exhibit systematic biases. Prior work has documented position, verbosity or model family of the candidate answers influencing the judge decision rather than their quality, while additional biases may remain undocumented. $\textit{Multicalibration}$ provides a natural framework to address this problem: each bias corresponds to miscalibration on an identifiable group, $\textit{e.g.}$, family bias manifests as overconfidence in answers generated by models belonging to the same family of the judge. The challenge is to fix miscalibration simultaneously across many, potentially unknown groups. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{CaLLM}$, a post hoc framework that multicalibrates an LLM judge, thereby bounding all such biases simultaneously. We prove that $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ bounds the bias of every group whose error structure is captured by an available representation, and that augmenting it with explicit bias groups further reduces the residual bias. We then derive theoretical conditions under which $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ improves the judge's accuracy, rather than trading it for calibration. Finally, we evaluate $\mathrm{CaLLM}$ across pairwise preference benchmarks, showing that it reduces the multicalibration error on both specified and unspecified bias groups, while improving predictive performance of the judge.

title: A Controlled Evaluation of Curvature Inspired Scalar Feature Scaling for Domain Generalization
summary: Domain-specific curvature is an appealing idea for domain generalization (DG), but curvature learning can denote substantially different computations. This paper evaluates one deliberately narrow implementation: the code calls it HyperDG, but it rescales Euclidean encoder features during training by learned positive scalars and uses an ordinary linear classifier on unscaled Euclidean features at inference. It does not implement a Lorentz or Poincaré representation, geodesic prediction, or a Sharpness-Aware Minimization inner loop. We audit the executed objective and evaluate six conditions on PACS, VLCS, Office Home, and TerraIncognita. The completed design contains 384 runs: six conditions, four held-out targets, and four run seeds per dataset. Checkpoints are selected using only the three source-validation environments. Inference first averages paired seed differences within each held-out target; targets, rather than 16 seed-by-target observations, are the per-dataset clusters. The full implementation's equal-dataset macro point estimate is 1.61 percentage points below native DomainBed ERM (95% clustered CI [-3.17, -0.04]). All four dataset point estimates favor ERM, but an exact four-dataset sign-flip test gives p = .125 and Holm-adjusted p = .250; we therefore claim no adjusted evidence of a difference. The cleaner domain-specificity contrast, separate learned source scales without their variance penalty versus one shared learned source scale, is -0.13 pp (95% CI [-0.53, 0.27]). Its 90% CI lies within a revision-stage $\pm 1$ pp smallest effect of practical interest (TOST p = .003), supporting equivalence only for the source-selected suite macro, not every dataset, target, or final-step endpoint. The study thus supplies a bounded negative result for this scalar training package; it does not test or refute genuine hyperbolic representation learning.

title: A Differentiable 3D Scene Graph Metric via Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry
summary: 3D scene graph prediction is commonly supervised with local object and predicate classification losses. Although effective for slot-wise label prediction, this formulation does not provide a graph-level semantic distance between a predicted scene graph and its ground truth: semantically mild label errors and structurally disruptive relational errors can be treated similarly, and subject-predicate-object facts are not compared as scene-level units. We propose Contextual Hellinger Triplet Geometry, a graph-level supervision objective that measures the semantic and structural discrepancy between 3D scene graphs. Our key idea is to reinterpret the conventional classifier outputs of a 3D scene graph predictor as an aligned probabilistic scene graph field, where object and predicate predictions jointly define contextual subject-predicate-object facts. This formulation yields a differentiable metric-based training objective with an efficient factorized implementation and can be applied to existing 3D scene graph prediction architectures without modifying their network design. Experiments on 3DSSG demonstrate that our supervision improves downstream graph-conditioned 3D scene generation, while ablation studies confirm the complementary roles of the proposed graph-level terms and user studies show better graph descriptiveness, relation plausibility, and structural preservation.

title: A Few More Tokens Ahead: Reinforcing Parallelism in Diffusion LLMs
summary: Parallel generation is widely regarded as an inherent advantage of diffusion large language models. Yet our fixed-quota evaluation of four representative models reveals severe degradation across mathematics and code, with all scores below 15% at 16 tokens per step. Token-level probes identify local predictive potential near the observed prefix, especially in mathematical text. We propose RePara, which reinforces short consecutive token blocks through group-relative policy optimization and reduces rollout and log-probability recomputation costs. On LLaDA and SDAR, \ours improves GSM8K and MATH-500 accuracy over JustGRPO under reduced denoising budgets, with a 1.96x training-step speedup in our LLaDA/MATH setup.

title: A Geometrical Approach to Constructing Neural Networks for Perfect Training-set Classification
summary: This paper proposes a method for constructing a neural network that achieves perfect classification of all samples in a given training set, without taking regularization into account. The network is constructed on-demand, with its layer sizes and neuron parameters determined through a geometrical analysis of the input data, in which separating hyperplanes are created and mapped to neurons with step activation functions. The proposed architecture consists of two hidden layers with distinct roles: inter-class separation and transformation of the data into a linearly separable representation. Inter-class separation requires every bi-chromatic pair of samples belonging to different classes to be separated by at least one hyperplane. We show that when this separation is achieved through a hierarchical partitioning of the data, the leaf nodes of the oblique decision tree, obtained as a byproduct, directly define the neurons of the linear separability layer, whose size is only one neuron greater than that of the inter-class separation layer. Experiments on the MNIST dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves perfect training-set classification, and compact models. The direct correspondence between the decision tree and network neurons enhances interpretability and explainability, while the construction procedure offers opportunities for parallel implementation and improved scalability.

title: A Global View of How LLMs Value Human Time
summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. These findings indicate that geographical patterns are embedded in LLMs and may translate in different treatment in agentic settings.

title: A Method for Exact Enforcement of Boundary Conditions on General Curved Triangular Domains: Algorithm and Application to Scientific Machine Learning
summary: We present a method for enforcing exactly Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on general triangular domains with arbitrarily curved boundaries. The algorithmic constructions developed here complements those in a previous work for general quadrilateral domains. Our method combines (i) the exact mapping between a general curved triangular domain and the standard triangle, (ii) TFC constrained expressions, and (iii) Barnhill transfinite interpolations, to provide explicit closed-form trial ansatze that mathematically satisfy the imposed boundary conditions exactly. Corner compatibility induced by the boundary conditions is pivotal, and enforcing exactly the imposed boundary conditions hinges on the exact enforcement of the induced compatibility constraints. The corner compatibility associated with the acute vertices of the standard triangle and the coupling between gradient components when the hypotenuse corresponds to a Neumann/Robin boundary pose particular challenges. Two strategies are critical to resolving these issues, by reformulating conditional corner constraints into equivalent unconditional forms and by introducing a separate TFC-style auxiliary edge construction together with an associated linear solve on the hypotenuse. We analyze the corner compatibility constraints and present formulations for the general form of functions that exactly satisfy the imposed Dirichlet, Neumann, or Robin conditions on curved triangular domains. The proposed method has been implemented using extreme learning machine type randomized neural networks for solving PDE problems. We present ample numerical experiments with linear/nonlinear PDE problems on a variety of domains with complex boundary geometries. Numerical results show that the current method has enforced the Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on curved domain boundaries to the machine precision.

title: A Node Embedding Framework for Model-Centric Conformance Checking in Process Mining
summary: Evaluating the quality of process models discovered from event logs is a fundamental challenge in process mining. Traditional evaluation relies on conformance metrics such as fitness and precision, which are highly sensitive to noise and deviations in event logs and therefore often fail to give a consistent assessment of discovery algorithms. We introduce a model-centric evaluation framework that combines node embeddings with Procrustes alignment to enable cross-graph comparability, since embeddings derived from different graphs reside in distinct vector spaces. The proposed PetriNetGraph method transforms Petri net process models into graph representations compatible with embedding algorithms. Comparing the node embeddings of ground-truth and discovered models through a parameterized cosine distance yields a unified and bounded metric for evaluating process discovery across datasets and methods. We evaluate the framework under static and context-aware scenarios to examine how prior knowledge of activity existence influences the assessment of structural similarity. The framework also integrates a compliance checking mechanism that localizes deviations at the activity level and an entropy-regularized node distance aggregation function that quantifies global deviations across the model. Experiments on nine publicly available event logs show that the approach provides a reliable embedding-based conformance indicator that reflects the behavior of fitness and precision. Experiments on synthetic logs with controlled noise levels confirm that it is substantially more robust to log deviations than traditional conformance metrics, PetriNet2Vec, and its dynamic-window and Procrustes-aligned variants, while remaining sensitive to process model degradation. All implementation details and datasets are publicly available.

title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
summary: We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. The method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and provides a way to establish convergence rates for new optimization algorithms through calculus arguments applied to their associated SDEs.

title: A Refresh Interval Does Not Fully Specify a Refresh Schedule: Learning-Rate-Dependent Placement in Kronecker-Preconditioned Language Model Training
summary: Kronecker-preconditioned optimizers recompute a cached curvature eigendecomposition only periodically, and implementations and adaptive methods control this through the refresh frequency. We show that frequency leaves part of a schedule free: at a fixed number of refreshes, when they occur changes held-out loss at the same compute. Training GPT-style models with the Mousse optimizer across model sizes, we move the middle refreshes of a four-refresh schedule while fixing the first and last. On FineWeb the two placements exchanged rank as the learning rate rose (later placement was better at low rates, earlier placement at high ones), so a single-learning-rate comparison can report either ranking. The reversal held under controls including the published optimizer internals, and placement still mattered at the published refresh density. The learning rate at which the preference flips fell with model size, consistent with a held-out smaller model, and shifted with training length. A spectral-width staleness score predicted the same ranking at every learning rate and missed the reversal. Refresh schedules should be reported in full and compared across the learning rates at which they will be used.

title: A Time-Synchronous Prequential Evaluation Framework for Next-Week Student Disengagement Prediction from Moodle LMS Logs
summary: Retrospective evaluation of early-warning models may not reflect information available when predictions are issued and outcomes become observable. We developed a time-synchronous prequential framework for online prediction of next-week student disengagement, operationalised as inactivity onset, from Moodle logs. Ordered by calendar time, models were updated only with available outcomes and remained unchanged for all predictions at each prediction cutoff; development, calibration and evaluation were chronologically separate. We compared stochastic gradient descent logistic regression (SGD-LR), online sequential extreme learning machine (OSELM) and echo state network (ESN) across predictive performance, fixed, frozen and rolling threshold policies, calendar-time variation and four behavioural feature sets. Held-out evaluation comprised 49,329 predictions with 37.68% inactivity-onset prevalence. Discrimination was similar (average precision 0.665-0.679; ROC-AUC 0.755-0.774). OSELM had the highest recall, SGD-LR the highest precision and specificity, and ESN the highest Matthews correlation coefficient and balanced accuracy. Lower thresholds increased recall and alert volume, whereas rolling adaptation did not improve MCC over frozen thresholds. Weekly performance and calibrated-probability distributions varied without sustained deterioration. During model selection, cumulative-and-temporal features achieved the highest individual-set AP, with modest gains from combining all feature groups. These findings indicate that streaming early-warning evaluation should consider calibration, threshold-dependent performance, alert burden and calendar-time variation alongside aggregate discrimination.

title: A Tutorial on Quantum Amplitude Embedding with Data Re-Uploading
summary: Amplitude embedding lets a variational quantum model read many classical features with few qubits, but the model output is then only a quadratic form in the normalized input. Data re-uploading, which encodes the input repeatedly between trainable blocks, can be used to enrich such a model. Because every additional upload of an amplitude embedding repeats a costly state preparation, the gain that an upload buys has to be known before the gates are spent. This tutorial thus addresses the problem of explaining what data re-uploading adds to an amplitude-embedded model and how large the gain is. We express sequential re-uploading and parallel re-uploading with two copies in one notation and show that each upload raises the reachable polynomial order by two. Under one trainable circuit family and one budget of trainable parameters, simulation results show that re-uploading raises the test coefficient of determination from 0.689 to between 0.883 and 0.975 on targets of order four and from 0.337 to between 0.642 and 0.783 on targets of order six, on all ten seeds. On a quadratic target and on handwritten digits, one upload remains the best choice, and every additional upload lowers the gate error that the classifier tolerates. These results help designers match the number of uploads to the polynomial order of the task at hand.

title: A dataset of formalised theorem statements from the Annals of Mathematics
summary: Recent progress in autoformalisation of mathematics using AI has been impressive. Measuring this progress requires datasets of formal statements that are both hard and trustworthy. We present AnnalsChallenge: 50 formalised theorem statements written by hand in Lean 4 using Mathlib. Each is the main result of a paper published in the Annals of Mathematics since 2020. Every formalisation was manually reviewed and then audited by AI. We release them without formalised proofs.

title: AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Imaging for Intraoperative Detection of Low-Grade Glioma: A Clinical Study
summary: Current image-guided neuronavigation techniques, such as intraoperative MRI and ultrasound, are limited by high costs, limited sensitivity and operational complexity. There is a clear need for more efficient systems to enhance intra-operative tumor detection and improve patient outcomes for intrinsic brain tumor resection. Whereas previous intraoperative brain HSI studies have predominantly investigated high-grade gliomas, glioblastomas, or mixed-grade cohorts, this clinical study focuses specifically on low-grade gliomas (LGGs). LGGs strongly resemble normal brain under white light conditions on the operative microscope. This study characterizes spectral differences between healthy and tumor tissue and provides a paired comparison of HSI- and RGB-based classification at matched tissue locations and under identical patient-level data splits. Tumor regions showed consistently lower reflectance, which may be associated with differences in hemoglobin concentration and oxygenation. A range of classification models was evaluated. The 3D CNN, which integrates spectral and spatial features, achieved the highest median ROC-AUC of 74.5%, compared with 67.9% for the spectral-only XGBoost model and 64.0% for the RGB-based model. These results support further investigation of HSI for low-grade glioma classification and quantify its performance relative to conventional RGB imaging in this cohort.

title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
summary: The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.

title: AM-Bench: Understanding Agents under Task Underspecification across Models and Harnesses
summary: Ambiguous or incomplete task specifications complicate both execution and clarification for language-model agents. Yet agents' responses to these information gaps remain poorly characterized across models and execution harnesses. We present AM-Bench, a benchmark built from 48 tasks adapted from Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Harness-Bench. Each task includes a fully specified reference and six variants spanning ambiguous or missing goals, context, and constraints. We evaluate every pairing of five models and four harnesses over 20,160 runs.
